summary: The r29 two-planar null-sum receiver is false if it assumes only bounded planar joint densities. For eps>0, independent planar densities equal to 1 on rectangles of dimensions eps by 1/eps have joint caps one, while T=U^2+2V(Z+W) has p_T(0)=2 log(1/eps)+1+2 log 2+eps^2/12. This is not a counterexample to QFORM: in the underlying independent cap-one coordinates the matrix spectrum is {sqrt(2),-sqrt(2),eps^2,0}, so only two eigenvalues are large. A correct null-sum receiver must retain product-projection/Gram/X-ray or equivalent original-coordinate volume provenance.
